children: By David Thomas, Mike Scarcella and Sara Merken

The churn of law firm partners trading one employer for another is picking up speed, according to data from recruiters and others, underscoring the vulnerabilities of a business model in which a firm's assets can walk out the door at any moment.

The abrupt collapse of Weil, Gotshal & Manges as partner defections accelerated offered a dramatic example. Its demise has unleashed another scramble for talent, with rival firms now competing for Weil lawyers in what one recruiter described as a “Wild West land grab.”
Legal recruiter Macrae tracked 1,571 partner moves among the 100 highest-grossing US law firms in the first 10 months of 2026, a 10% increase over all of last year.

Firm Prospects, which tracks lateral activity, also said by the end of October, movement among all attorneys at the 200 highest-grossing US law firms had already surpassed 2025. The company tracked 3,228 lateral partner moves in the first three quarters of 2026, a 14% increase over the same period in 2025. Including counsel, associates and other lawyers, the increase was 20%.

To be sure, the days when most lawyers could be expected to spend their careers at a single law firm faded long ago. But recruiters said the latest surge in lateral movement highlights a deeper shift, where firms increasingly rely on poaching from rivals to fuel growth even as the same competition makes it easier for their own top lawyers to leave.
The heightened activity reflects a paradox: Firms must maintain growth to ward off a spiral if key partners leave, but the race to scale up increases the lateral pressures they continually face.
"Any firm that relies on the star system and doesn’t have the scale that is needed to insulate itself from one or two stars leaving, that firm is vulnerable," said Macrae partner Matthew Bersani.
The rise of outsized pay packages for top partners has helped drive the trend, Bersani said, as firms created bonus pools or revised their compensation systems to lure lateral rainmakers more easily.

Reports of compensation guarantees reaching $20 million or more create their own momentum, pushing partners to explore their own options, said Dave Maurer, global executive director for partner recruiting at Major, Lindsey & Africa.
"It gets people’s attention," he said.
AI STARTUP PERPLEXITY WITHDRAWS BID TO KEEP LAW FIRM PROSKAUER IN REDDIT LAWSUIT

Artificial intelligence startup Perplexity AI has withdrawn its bid for a court order allowing law firm Proskauer Rose to represent it in a lawsuit brought by Reddit, which is seeking to disqualify the firm over an alleged conflict.

In a filing this week in federal court in Manhattan, Perplexity said it no longer sought the order for Proskauer to appear as its counsel. The filing did not provide a reason, and Perplexity and Proskauer did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Proskauer has
that Reddit had no basis to disqualify ​the firm.

Reddit asked US District Judge Paul Engelmayer to block Proskauer from appearing, asserting the firm had earlier represented Reddit in a related matter. "Proskauer cannot drop Reddit like a hot potato in favor ⁠of Perplexity," Reddit said in its filing. Reddit, represented by law firm Bartlit Beck, declined to comment.
GOODWIN MATCHES MILBANK ON ASSOCIATE SALARIES

Goodwin Procter is increasing salaries for US associates, joining a small but growing list of firms to adjust associate compensation following Milbank’s raises earlier this year. Goodwin is also handing out two categories of bonuses.
Base salaries at Goodwin will range from $235,000 to $455,000 based on seniority, according to an internal memo that was viewed by Reuters.

“This reflects our continued investment in you, our commitment to rewarding your work, and our focus on keeping our compensation among the most competitive in the market,” Goodwin managing partner Josh Klatzkin said in the memo. The raises take effect in January.

Milbank, which in recent years has been a first mover among large law firms on associate compensation, announced salary increases in ‌June. A handful of firms including McDermott, Will & Schulte matched at the time. Firms such as Sheppard, Mullin, Richter & Hampton, Winston Taylor and Cooley have in recent weeks matched the new salary scale.

Milbank also rolled out so-called special bonuses of up to $25,000 in July. Goodwin’s memo said the firm will pay the same special bonus scale, in addition to standard annual bonuses based on class year to associates who meet a certain billable hours threshold.
